clue.text: Some music on LP? Not a note

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it, so the music comes after the coin value

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50, and P is the usual abbreviation for pence, the British penny coin
a piece is a single composition or work of music

explanation.surface: A wry comment that a long-playing record holds only a little music and somehow lacks a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LP' looks like a vinyl album but is read letter by letter: L = 50 and P = pence. The 'note' of the definition is a banknote, not a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: The coin is cash that is not paper money: a cryptic way of describing a British coin worth half a pound rather than a banknote.

clue.text: Person catching extremists in Ferrari with tank

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its outermost letters, here the first and last of Ferrari

parts.note: the Sherman was an American tank of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Someone apprehended while driving a Ferrari with a fuel tank, or with an armoured tank in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is literally a person who spends the day catching fish, so the bare phrase describes the occupation.

clue.text: Coming up, vulgar features mainly lacking inspiration, initially, for cinephile

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
a thing that features something includes it, so the vulgar word holds the initials inside it

parts.note: naff is British slang for tacky or vulgar

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the three words mainly, lacking and inspiration

explanation.surface: A cinema-lover complains that vulgar films lack inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' looks like films but is the container signal: MLI goes inside NAFF to make NAFMLIF, which 'Coming up' turns round. NAFF is British slang for tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinephile is a devotee of cinema, i.e. a lover of movies.

clue.text: Once upon a time, finish off gravy with a bit of corn starch

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, here the end of gravy

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant such as corn
sago is a starch from palm pith, used in puddings

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: once, you would finish gravy by stirring in some cornstarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once upon a time' looks like a fairy-tale opening attached to the cooking, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means long in the past, the same sense as the storyteller's opening.

clue.text: Gobbled up by Lancelot, a really lovely lyrist

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the swallowed letters read from bottom to top
letters gobbled by these words are swallowed inside them, running across Lancelot, a and really

explanation.surface: Sir Lancelot falls for a beautiful poet and devours her songs.
explanation.definitionFit: The muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek myth, so a beautiful lyrist.

clue.text: Something turning up on female garment — unpleasant discovery there?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it
in a down answer, up means the curve is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an arc is a curve, a line that turns
a blouse is a woman's shirt

explanation.surface: Something crawling up on a woman's blouse: an unpleasant find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to the female garment: the parasite is the nasty find in the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pubic parasite found in clothing or bedding would indeed be a nasty discovery, so the definition hints by context.

clue.text: Bum parts outside of pants, moon!

indicators.note: the tramp parts the two letters, splitting them by sitting between
the outside of a word is its first and last letters, here of pants

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant, a hobo

explanation.surface: A schoolboy prank: bottom out of the trousers, mooning someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' and 'moon' suggest a bare bottom, but Bum is a tramp and moon is the definition, the larger satellite of Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the larger of the two natural satellites of Mars.

clue.text: Remove hairs from bottom of hirsute old governor

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of hirsute

parts.note: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judaea at the time of the Crucifixion

explanation.surface: A depilation job on the backside of a hairy ancient governor.
explanation.definitionFit: To depilate or strip the body of unwanted growth, a beauty-salon verb.

clue.text: Correct tip overwhelms this chap

indicators.note: the tip swamps the chap by closing round him

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
the setter speaking of himself, so me

explanation.surface: A hot tip on a race proves too much for the speaker, in an oddly corrected sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend or revise a text is to put it right.

clue.text: Wife of leader, a shade insular, briefly?

indicators.note: the placing is really done by the in at the front of insular; this little word only links the shade to it
briefly trims the word: the in at its front is used up as the placing word and the end letter is docked

parts.note: taken as written; Paul reads it as in followed by the rest of its letters
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A leader's wife is a touch narrow-minded, to put it briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: A trick split: 'insular' reads as the containment word 'in' followed by the letters that receive the shade; 'briefly' docks the last of those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife of an Islamic ruler such as a sultan carries this title.

clue.text: Time to welcome revolutionary Chinese brood

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the age surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the Chinese prefix reads backwards

parts.note: Sino- is the combining form meaning Chinese

explanation.surface: Time to welcome a brood of young Chinese revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' looks like a noun, a family of young, but it is the verb: to worry over something.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to worry and fret at length, the same sense as agonising.

clue.text: A little angel, free spirit

indicators.note: a little of the words angel free is a short stretch of their letters

explanation.surface: A small cherub, a carefree being.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite of folklore, a small supernatural being.

clue.text: Person with load unsure about weight that's an ounce

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the weight
being unsure means wobbly and unsettled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a load is uncertain whether it weighs an ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounce' looks like a unit of weight, but it is also a name for a big cat of the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is an old name for the big cat of the Central Asian mountains, a pale spotted cat.

clue.text: Faithful cat carrying on with a meal for him, shortly?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the cat takes the next word inside

parts.note: mog or moggie is British slang for a cat
taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a cat's meal: the rodent it catches

explanation.surface: A loyal cat carries on with a light meal set for its master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on with' suggests an affair, the opposite of the definition. MOG is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Having only one partner is being faithful to a spouse.

clue.text: Person proposing to install creation of iron that's more than a mile wide

indicators.note: to install means to put in place inside, so the mover holds the other letters

parts.note: a mover is the person who proposes a motion at a meeting

indicators.note: a creation of the word iron is something made from it, a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone proposing to install an iron structure that spans over a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the song from Breakfast at Tiffany's: 'wider than a mile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mancini–Mercer song opens by describing the stream as wider than a mile.

clue.text: One side not quite covering a page

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so the shortened side holds the a
not quite means falling short by the final letter

parts.note: left is one side, as against right

explanation.surface: One side only partly covers a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A single sheet in a book, printed on both sides, is also called a page.

clue.text: Texas city out to impress couple on tour, ultimately

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the out word takes the couple inside

parts.note: forth means out, as in 'go forth'
a couple is two

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of tour

explanation.surface: A Texan city goes out of its way to impress a touring couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in north Texas, neighbour of Dallas.

clue.text: Number a hundred I book up for a wink or a kiss, say?

definitions.text: a wink or a kiss, say?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone counting their books, sending a hundred winks and kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: Typed symbols like ;) or x represent a wink or a kiss, so both are examples of this smiley-type icon.

clue.text: Cops stopping method by corruption, finally

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are set next to each other
finally points to the last letter of corruption

parts.note: ABS, anti-lock braking system, is a way of stopping a car

explanation.surface: Police officers halting a corrupt practice in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' looks like a noun, the police, but it is the verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop or nab someone are both slang for arrest or catch.

clue.text: Keeping mum suspiciously, French produce English citizen

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the cheese surrounds the other letters

parts.note: brie is a French cheese

indicators.note: acting suspiciously is acting oddly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An English citizen suspiciously keeps quiet about French produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like 'silent' or 'mother' but is just the letters jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Birmingham, England's second city, is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Mile covered by person propelling boat near Brighton? Type of cutter

parts.note: Hove is the town next to Brighton on the English south coast

indicators.note: covered by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: a rower drives a boat with oars

explanation.surface: A rower covering a mile off the Sussex coast.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is the seaside town next to Brighton. 'cutter' suggests a boat to go with the rower, but it is a lawn cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-cutting machine riding on a cushion of air is one sort of lawn cutter.

clue.text: Ride Disney duck, kicking tail

parts.note: Walt Disney, the film-maker

indicators.note: kicking means getting rid of, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought

explanation.surface: Donald Duck at a Disney theme park, losing his tail on a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disney duck' suggests Donald, but Disney gives WALT and duck is the cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground ride with spinning cars is a kind of carnival attraction.

clue.text: Explosion of octane now

indicators.note: an explosion blows the word octane apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Petrol vapour about to blow up immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Fraction on calculator opposite number

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a counter is something that calculates or tallies
a part is a fraction of the whole

explanation.surface: Doing sums: a fraction typed on a calculator and its opposite number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite number' sounds mathematical but means a person's equivalent elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding the equivalent post in another organisation is their equal.

clue.text: In trolley, a gold weight

indicators.note: in places the a inside the trolley word

parts.note: a cart is a trolley

explanation.surface: A shopping trolley carrying a gold weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit measuring gold purity and gemstone mass, two hundred milligrams for jewels.

clue.text: Every other bit of Paul hairy: my fear!

indicators.note: every other letter is picked, starting with the second, through Paul, hairy and my

explanation.surface: The setter, Paul, horrified at the thought of being hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden fright or apprehension.

clue.text: Little moo

definitions.meaning: little means small or short in height
a moo is the sound cattle make, in the old sense also a verb for cows calling

explanation.definitionFit: Small in height is one sense and a bovine bellow is another.

clue.text: Dropping back, wander round country house in Russia

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the country
dropping the back of a word removes its last letter

parts.note: to rove is to wander
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A wanderer drifts round a country estate in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a building, but it means a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The last imperial dynasty of Russia was this royal family.

clue.text: Leaving America, a poor beggar clutching cup's heading for a Moorish palace

indicators.note: clutching means holding within
the abbreviation for America leaves the beggar's name

parts.note: Lazarus is the poor beggar of the parable of the rich man

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, here of cup's

explanation.surface: A poor beggar quits America holding a cup, bound for a palace in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The beggar is Lazarus of Luke's Gospel; 'for' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish fortress-palace of Moorish build, such as the one in Seville.

clue.text: Charles the Second marrying subject, harmony with CIIR restored

parts.note: a theme is a subject

indicators.note: restored means put back in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as C, II R: C and two Rs, the II meaning a pair

explanation.surface: King Charles II marries his subject, harmony restored to the royal monogram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CIIR' looks like Charles II Rex but is read C + two Rs; with HARMONY those letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname given to King Charles II of England for his pleasure-loving court.
